title: Kingdom of Numidia
capsule: Numidia was the Berber kingdom of North Africa stretching across what is now northern Algeria, unified by Masinissa of the Massylii in 202 BCE after he allied with Rome against Carthage in the Second Punic War. At its apex under Masinissa and his son Micipsa, the kingdom was a major grain exporter and patron of Hellenistic culture, with its capital at Cirta. The succession crisis that followed Micipsa's death produced the Jugurthine War (112–105 BCE), which ended with Jugurtha's capture through treachery by the Mauretanian king Bocchus and handover to Rome; the kingdom survived as a Roman client state until Julius Caesar partitioned it into the province of Africa Nova in 46 BCE.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The kingdom's approximate territorial outline is documented in Greek and Roman texts and corroborated by inscription distribution, though interior frontiers are inferred rather than precisely mapped.
